A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same two-layer linear model, exact solution, phase diagrams, and shared experiments. The complete main texts and Appendices A and B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment simulations, CIFAR-10 experiments with ResNet-18 and two-layer networks, and an appendix comparison of SGD and Adam.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulations and CIFAR-10 results and adds experiments with additional activations, deeper networks on MNIST, and synthetic binary classification.

M1.justification: The analyzed model remains a two-layer linear network trained by gradient flow on squared loss, with separate layer learning rates and arbitrary initialization. The additional nonlinear and deeper networks are empirical tests, not changes to the proposed analytical model or training procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds MNIST image classification and classification of samples from two Gaussian distributions, N(0,1) and N(4,1), in Figures 2, 6, and 7. Synthetic regression and CIFAR-10 remain, so coverage expands within the existing supervised-learning scope.

E2.justification: The SGD–Adam comparison under Xavier+ and Kaiming+ initialization in v1 Figure 5 and Appendix B.1 is removed. The corresponding CIFAR-10 comparison still includes NTK, mean field, Kaiming±, and Xavier±. RMSProp was discussed but not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce substantial evaluation designs: additional activation functions, four- and six-layer networks, a matrix-based alignment measure, and binary cross-entropy classification. The MNIST experiments use full-batch GD with batch size 2000 to control for SGD's alignment bias, selecting learning rates for convergence within 1000 iterations. The retained CIFAR-10 protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens tests of the alignment mechanism across activations, network depth, initialization scale, and regression versus classification losses (Figures 1, 2, 6, and 7). These directly examine generality beyond v1's linear/ReLU toy demonstrations and indirect ResNet evidence. The optimizer-sensitivity analysis in v1 Figure 5 is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. The theoretical distributions of initialization quantities are retained and do not constitute experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds alignment trajectories for sigmoid, swish, and leaky ReLU, depth and initialization results on MNIST, and classification findings including departures from perfect alignment under non-ReLU activations. The SGD–Adam results disappear. Matched CIFAR-10 curves and their reported approximately 5% and 10% accuracy gaps remain unchanged; the expansion does not establish improved performance under those settings.

T1.justification: v2 adds a matrix alignment definition and a derivation bounding final alignment away from zero under stated feature-learning conditions in Section 4. The existing one-dimensional loss reduction becomes Proposition 1 with an expanded Appendix A.1 proof, whose equations omit the averaging factor and squared-loss notation. The main exact-solution theorem, phase theorem, and corollaries are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows analysis of 'all possible limits' to 'different limits' and explicitly states empirical applicability to deep nonlinear networks. The central contributions—an exact finite-width solution with arbitrary initialization and three feature-learning mechanisms absent from the kernel phase—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 removes the adaptive-optimizer interpretation and adds explanations involving initialization-dependent GD–SGD differences, hyperparameter transfer, and large initialization entering the kernel regime. The conclusion replaces planned exploration beyond one-dimensional inputs with speculation about impossibility and drops the statement that alignment findings are preliminary. The core alignment, norm, and generalization interpretation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly specifies the regression sampling distribution and noise scale and documents initialization, loss, and training-selection details for the added experiments. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained regression setup. CIFAR-10 hyperparameters and the ResNet implementation pointer remain unchanged; exact learning rates for the new tests are not supplied.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section substantially expands positioning against finite-width corrections, mean-field analyses, and deep-linear-network theory. Added references include Braun et al. on exact dynamics with prior knowledge, Bordelon and Pehlevan on finite-width fluctuations, and Yang et al. on hyperparameter transfer. It explicitly distinguishes perturbative or special-initialization results from the paper's exact arbitrary-initialization solution.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten, related work becomes a dedicated section, and the solution presentation is reorganized around a proposition and appendix proof. Explanations are condensed or revised throughout, alongside changes to the title and affiliations. This is a substantial narrative reorganization beyond renumbering or local copyediting.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from four panels to a ten-panel activation comparison with shared legends and revised axes. New Figures 2, 6, and 7 display depth and classification analyses, while v1's optimizer figure is removed. Retained CIFAR-10 figures and Table 1 are resized or relocated, and the table caption moves above the table.

improvement.justification: Direct layer measurements on MNIST and the activation/loss checks strengthen support beyond v1's shallow demonstrations and indirect ResNet norm evidence. Expanded related work also clarifies the contribution. These gains outweigh the removed optimizer analysis, but the new Appendix A.1 proof introduces averaging and squared-loss inconsistencies, limiting the net improvement.
